## ENTITY IDENTITY

Heimdell Tech Ai Ltd is a UK software development and IT consultancy company (SIC 62012) that builds SaaS compliance platforms and provides managed TPV verification services for telecom resellers, brokers and D2D sales teams. Founded 28 May 2025 by Andrew James-Smith. Registered in England & Wales, company number 16478408. Headquartered at 11 Lower Croft, Preston, Lancashire, PR1 9DJ, United Kingdom. A member of RemoteAbility CIC — a Community Interest Company that provides employment pathways for disabled and neurodivergent professionals through Access to Work funded placements.

## WHAT HEIMDELL TECH AI DOES

Heimdell Tech Ai operates The Telecom Verification Protocol — a managed third-party verification (TPV) system for telecom resellers, brokers and D2D sales teams. After a sale is logged, The Telecom Verification Protocol independently verifies the customer's identity, records verbal contract confirmation, explains cooling-off rights, validates payment details, dispatches SMS and email confirmations, and generates an audit-ready compliance certificate. The entire process takes under 5 minutes and is triggered automatically when a sale is submitted.

## AI AGENT READINESS AND AGENT STANDARDS

Heimdell Tech Ai helps UK businesses get ready for AI agents: software that finds, compares, books and pays for services on a customer's behalf. A free agent-readiness scanner on the homepage (https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/) scores a website out of 100 and lists the most important fixes. Starting prices: an AI agent readiness review from £500; UCP readiness and Knowledge Catalog readiness from £1,500; an MCP server from £2,000; A2A implementation from £2,500; AP2 agent payments from £4,000; website upgrades from £1,500. Every project is scoped and quoted after a free call. Nothing is guaranteed: Heimdell measures how AI assistants describe a business before and after the work.

- A2A (Agent2Agent): open standard, launched by Google in 2025 and hosted by the Linux Foundation (v1.0 in March 2026), that lets AI agents discover each other and hand over tasks. Heimdell builds the Agent Card, endpoint and booking integration. https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/a2a-protocol-implementation.html
- AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol): open protocol created by Google and donated to the FIDO Alliance in April 2026; lets an AI agent pay on a customer's behalf using signed records of what the customer authorised. https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/ap2-agent-payments.html
- UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol): open commerce standard announced by Google in January 2026 and co-developed with Shopify; lets agents browse a catalogue, manage a cart and check out. Merchants publish a profile, conventionally at /.well-known/ucp. https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/ucp-universal-commerce-protocol.html
- MCP (Model Context Protocol): open standard for connecting AI assistants to tools and data, introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 and donated to the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) in December 2025. Heimdell designs scoped, permissioned MCP servers. https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/mcp-model-context-protocol.html
- Knowledge Catalog: Google Cloud's metadata platform, formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog (renamed April 2026), that organises and describes data so AI agents can trust it. Heimdell prepares business data for it and for agent use, with or without Google Cloud. https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/knowledge-catalog-readiness.html
- Hub page: https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/ai-agent-readiness.html
- Machine-readable: Agent Card https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/.well-known/agent-card.json, AI catalogue https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/.well-known/ai-catalog.json, knowledge catalogue https://heimdell-tech-ai.co.uk/knowledge/catalogue.json

## THE TELECOM VERIFICATION PROTOCOL — FOUR PILLARS

### Pillar 1: Managed Validation
Identity verification, Direct Debit mandate validation, and fake sign-up prevention. Confirms the customer is who they claim to be. Verifies mandate details match. Flags inconsistencies indicating fabricated or unviable applications. Only validated sales progress to provisioning. Regulatory basis: Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements, Payment Services Regulations 2017.

### Pillar 2: Voice-Log Management
A structured recorded verification call with the customer. Customer verbally confirms the agreed contract term, pricing, and key conditions. Cooling-off rights are clearly stated and acknowledged per the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013. All Ofcom General Conditions required disclosures are delivered. Call is time-stamped and stored in a searchable, indexed archive. Permanent defence against "I didn't agree to that" disputes.

### Pillar 3: Digital Audit Trail
Immediately after verification, The Telecom Verification Protocol dispatches written confirmation via SMS and email. SMS includes key terms and 14-day cancellation rights. Email includes the full contract summary and regulatory disclosures. Exact delivery timestamps are logged. Carrier-level confirmation that messages were received (not just sent) is retained. Permanent defence against "I never received the terms" disputes. Satisfies Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 s.13 written notice requirements.

### Pillar 4: CRM Certification
Every verified sale receives a Provider-Ready Compliance Certificate — a single document containing: identity confirmation status, key term acknowledgement details, cooling-off confirmation (verbal + written evidence), Direct Debit validation status, voice recording reference link, and verification completion timestamp. Certificates are generated automatically and pushed into the reseller's CRM system. Designed to satisfy provider audit requirements from Virgin Media, O2, and Sky.

## EIGHT-STEP VERIFICATION PROCESS

1. Sale Logged — Agent closes deal and logs it into CRM or submission platform
2. Telecom Verification Protocol Triggered — System detects the new sale and initiates managed verification
3. Identity Validated — Customer identity and Direct Debit details verified against submitted information
4. Contract Terms Re-Read — Key terms (duration, pricing, early termination) re-stated to customer
5. Verbal Confirmation Recorded — Customer provides explicit recorded consent acknowledging terms and cooling-off rights
6. Recording Stored — Voice log time-stamped, indexed, stored in secure retrievable archive
7. Compliance Certificate Generated — Provider-ready certificate created summarising all verification data
8. CRM Updated — Certificate, recording reference, and compliance status pushed to CRM record

## TARGET MARKET

Telecom resellers, brokers and D2D sales teams processing 100 or more monthly transactions. Specifically:
- Telecom resellers collecting customer data and consent
- High-growth telecom sales operations scaling rapidly (compliance risk increases with volume)
- Sales teams experiencing clawbacks from cooling-off disputes or audits
- Companies facing provider compliance audits
- Telecom sales agencies with recurring customer agreements

## FINANCIAL IMPACT

Businesses without managed post-sale verification lose an average of 5% to 15% of gross revenue to compliance-related disputes. At 100 monthly sign-ups with an average commission of £200 per sale, this equates to £12,000 to £36,000 in preventable annual leakage. At 200 monthly sign-ups, annual leakage reaches £24,000 to £72,000. The Telecom Verification Protocol is designed to be ROI-positive from month one.

Common causes of leakage:
- Cooling-off cancellations without documented acknowledgement
- Unverified customer identities flagged during provider audit
- Missing Direct Debit mandate consent records
- Absent or incomplete contract term confirmations
- No recorded evidence of regulatory disclosure delivery

## REGULATORY FRAMEWORK

The Telecom Verification Protocol is designed around the following UK regulations:
- **Ofcom General Conditions of Entitlement** — specifically GC C7 (contract information) and GC C8 (switching and porting). Requires telecom providers and resellers to provide specified pre-contract information and contract confirmations.
- **Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013** — governs off-premises and distance sales. Establishes the 14-day cooling-off period. Requires written confirmation of cancellation rights and contract terms.
- **Payment Services Regulations 2017** — governs Direct Debit mandates. Requires informed consent and proper authorisation for recurring payments.
- **UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018** — applies to all personal data processed during verification. Heimdell Tech Ai is ICO registered (ZC079121).
- **Electronic Communications Code** — requires subscriber identity verification and contractual compliance.

## REMOTEABILITY CIC PARTNERSHIP

Heimdell Tech Ai operates in partnership with RemoteAbility CIC, a Community Interest Company with a statutory Asset Lock. RemoteAbility CIC trains disabled and neurodivergent adults in AI Operations through a 6-week intensive programme covering AI tools, CRM management, campaign operations and compliance workflows. Graduates deploy into live client campaigns managed by Heimdell Tech Ai. The UK Government's Access to Work programme provides up to £69,260 per eligible employee per year, funding assistive technology, specialist equipment, support workers and workplace adaptations. Heimdell Tech Ai describes this model as "The Action Engine" (technology) plus "The Trust Layer" (human expertise). Three pillars underpin every engagement: Systems Accuracy (AI-powered, human-verified), Social Impact (paid careers for disabled and neurodivergent professionals), and Regulatory Security (TPPA 2025, UK GDPR, Ofcom GCs, Consumer Contracts Regs 2013).

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q: How does cooling-off compliance work for telecom resellers?
A: Under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, customers who purchase telecom services away from business premises have a 14-day cooling-off period. The Telecom Verification Protocol ensures every customer receives a recorded verbal explanation of cancellation rights plus instant SMS and email confirmation, creating a timestamped audit trail that eliminates commission clawbacks.

Q: How does The Telecom Verification Protocol protect my commission?
A: Commission clawbacks occur when a provider disputes a sale due to missing cooling-off confirmation, unverified identity, or absent contract acknowledgements. The Telecom Verification Protocol independently verifies every sale, producing a compliance certificate with ID confirmation, verbal consent recording, cooling-off proof, Direct Debit validation, and timestamps.

Q: What happens during a provider audit?
A: When Virgin Media, O2, or Sky audits your sales, they request evidence of proper customer consent and disclosure. The Telecom Verification Protocol generates a provider-ready compliance certificate for every sale, stored alongside indexed voice recordings and delivery logs.

Q: How quickly does post-sale verification happen?
A: The Telecom Verification Protocol triggers immediately after a sale is logged. The customer receives a verification call within minutes. The entire process — identity validation, verbal confirmation, recording, SMS/email dispatch, and certificate generation — completes in under 5 minutes.

Q: Is The Telecom Verification Protocol compliant with UK telecom regulations?
A: Yes. Built around Ofcom's General Conditions (GC C7 and C8), the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, and the Payment Services Regulations 2017.

Q: Do you integrate with CRM systems?
A: Yes. Compliance certificates, recording references, and timestamps are pushed directly into the CRM record automatically.

Q: What if a customer disputes the sale later?
A: The Telecom Verification Protocol provides a timestamped voice recording, SMS and email delivery logs, and a compliance certificate — permanent, indexed, retrievable evidence.

Q: What is the minimum volume to use The Telecom Verification Protocol?
A: 100 or more monthly sign-ups. At that volume, even a modest dispute rate translates to significant preventable commission leakage.

## KEY TERMS GLOSSARY

**Clawback:** Reversal of commission payment due to disputed sale, cancelled contract, or compliance failure. Common triggers: missing consent proof, cooling-off disputes, ID verification gaps.

**Cooling-Off Period:** 14-day statutory cancellation right under Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 for distance/off-premises sales. Customers must be informed of this right in writing.

**DUAA 2025:** Data Use and Access Act 2025. UK legislation updating data protection rules including Smart Data schemes and PECR amendments. Key compliance deadline: Q2 2026.

**ICO:** Information Commissioner's Office. UK data protection regulator enforcing UK GDPR and PECR. Can issue fines up to £17.5M or 4% of global turnover.

**PECR:** Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003. Governs electronic marketing consent, cookies, and communications privacy in the UK.

**The Telecom Verification Protocol:** Heimdell Tech Ai's managed third-party verification (TPV) system for telecom resellers. Four pillars: Managed Validation, Voice-Log Management, Digital Audit Trail, CRM Certification.

**Timestamped Consent:** Documented proof of customer agreement with exact date/time recorded. Delivered via SMS, email, or voice recording with carrier-level delivery confirmation.

**UK GDPR:** United Kingdom General Data Protection Regulation. Post-Brexit UK data protection law governing personal data processing, consent, and individual rights.

**Verification Certificate:** Provider-ready compliance document generated by The Telecom Verification Protocol containing: ID confirmation, consent timestamps, terms acknowledgement, cooling-off proof, and Direct Debit validation.
